level_1: Identifies categories of reconstruction options
Manages acute complications from low- complexity reconstruction
Performs high- complexity, multi-staged reconstruction
level_2: Performs linear closures

Assists with management of long- term complications with surgical treatments
level_3: Manages complications from linear closures
Performs high-complexity reconstruction

level_1: Discusses en face sectioning and the process for preparing tissue for frozen section
Identifies normal variants, less common tumors, and high-risk features on frozen section
level_2: Identifies straightforward tumors on frozen section
Troubleshoots slides and suggests technical solutions
level_3: Assesses a Mohs slide competently for the presence/absence of tumor
Identifies unexpected findings, and rare and unusual tumors on frozen section
level_4: Identifies artifacts on frozen section
Prepares frozen section slides
level_5: Identifies when a recut is needed
Interprets frozen immunohistochemistry stains

level_1: Diagnoses and manages common malignant lesions and discusses current staging systems
Selects and manages alternative treatment and/or adjuvant therapy or work-up in addition to or in place of surgery
level_2: Discusses risks and benefits of non-surgical management options
Diagnoses and manages rare and unusual malignant lesions
level_3: Orders additional diagnostic testing to narrow the differential diagnosis or for staging
Coordinates multidisciplinary care for non-surgical management
level_4: Identifies patients who would benefit from non- surgical management
Prescribes novel non- surgical treatment options
level_5: Diagnoses and manages complex malignant lesions and stages tumor

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of surgically relevant normal anatomy and physiology, and principles of wound healing
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of surgically relevant anatomic variations and peri-operative considerations
level_3: With assistance, identifies surgically relevant anatomic variations and peri-operative considerations, and alters patient management accordingly
level_4: Independently identifies surgically relevant anatomic considerations and peri-operative considerations, and alters patient management accordingly
level_5: Significantly contributes to the surgical curriculum for a dermatology residency program or micrographic surgery and dermatologic oncology fellowship

level_1: Demonstrates basic knowledge of cutaneous oncology
level_2: Demonstrates comprehensive knowledge of cutaneous oncology and clinical implications
level_3: With assistance, applies knowledge of common cutaneous oncology into medical decision making
level_4: Independently incorporates knowledge of complex cutaneous oncology into medical decision making
level_5: Recommends novel investigations based on knowledge of cutaneous oncology and clinical trials

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common safety events
Describes local quality improvement initiatives
Discloses patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to safety events
Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
Mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems
Conducts analysis of safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Identifies specific population and community health needs for the local population
Advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems, including outpatient settings
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations, effectively using the roles of the interprofessional team members
Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations, effectively using the roles of the interprofessional team members
Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Leads effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties
Leads innovations and advocates for populations and communities with health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system
Describes core administrative knowledge needed for transition to practice
Advocates for patient care needs with consideration of the limitations of each patient’s payment models
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems and practice models
Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system
Analyzes individual practice patterns and professional requirements in preparation for practice
level_3: Identifies basic practice management knowledge domains for effective transition to practice
Engages with patients in shared decision making, informed by each patient’s payment models
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care
level_4: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Demonstrates use of information technology required for medical practice
Participates in health policy advocacy activities
level_5: Delivers care with consideration of each patient’s payment models
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care
Educates others to prepare them for transition to practice

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge that laboratories must be accredited
Discusses implications of proficiency testing failures
level_2: Discusses the need for quality control and proficiency testing
Participates in an internal or external laboratory inspection (actual or simulated)
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of the components of laboratory accreditation and regulatory compliance, either through training or experience
Performs analysis and review of proficiency testing failures and recommends a course of action, with oversight
level_4: Interprets quality data, charts, and trends, including proficiency testing results, with supervision
Independently formulates a response for proficiency testing failures
level_5: Identifies the differences between accreditation and regulatory compliance; discusses the process for achieving accreditation and maintaining regulatory compliance

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence, and incorporate patient preferences and values in order to take care of a routine patient
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence, even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence, to guide care tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients, and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Designs and implements a learning plan with prompting
Challenges own assumptions and considers alternatives in narrowing the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_2: Identifies the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Seeks performance data episodically, with adaptability and humility
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and, when necessary, improves it
level_3: Actively seeks opportunities to improve
Analyzes, reflects on, and institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Role models consistently seeking performance data with adaptability and humility
level_4: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to inform goals
Independently creates and implements a learning plan
Coaches others on reflective practice
level_5: Analyzes and reflects on the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Intentionally and consistently seeks performance data, with adaptability and humility
Facilitates the design and implementing learning plans for others

level_1: Identifies and describes potential triggers for professionalism lapses
Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas
level_2: Describes when and how to appropriately report professionalism lapses, including strategies for addressing common barriers
Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of medical ethical principles
Recognizes the need to seek help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution
level_4: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations
Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles
Serves as resource for colleagues who face ethical dilemmas
level_5: Takes responsibility for one’s own professionalism lapses
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself and others

level_1: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks
Recognizes situations that may impact one’s own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_2: Proactively ensures that the needs of patients are met
Mitigates situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Performs routine tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail
Implements strategies to enhance accountability of team members involved in patient care
level_4: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities
Takes ownership of system outcomes and suggests revisions to the systems to enhance accountability
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations

level_1: Recognizes status of personal and professional well-being, with assistance
Proposes a plan to remediate or improve limits in one’s own knowledge/skills
level_2: Recognizes limits in one’s own knowledge/ skills, with assistance
Independently develops and implements a plan to optimize personal and professional well- being
level_3: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being
Independently develops and implements a plan to remediate or improve limits in one’s own knowledge/skills
level_4: Independently recognizes limits in own knowledge/skills and seeks help when appropriate
Coaches others to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_5: Proposes a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being

level_1: Uses language and non- verbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport with patients of different backgrounds
Identifies the importance of engaging in shared decision making
Independently recognizes biases while attempting to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_2: Identifies common barriers (e.g., language, disability/hearing) to effective communication
Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging patient encounters, with guidance
Independently uses shared decision making to make a personalized care plan
level_3: Identifies elements of shared decision making
When prompted, reflects on biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection to consistently develop positive therapeutic relationships
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters using active listening and clear language
Uses shared decision making to make a personalized care plan, with guidance
Independently uses shared decision making to make a personalized care plan when there is a high degree of uncertainty
level_5: Identifies complex barriers (e.g., health literacy) to effective communication

level_1: Recognizes when a consultation is needed
Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Communicates feedback and constructive criticism to superiors
level_2: Respectfully receives a consultation request
Confirms comprehension of consultant recommendations
Role models flexible communication strategies that demonstrate one values input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed
level_3: Uses language that demonstrates that one values all members of the health care team
Checks understanding of recommendations when providing consultation
Facilitates regular health care team-based feedback in complex situations
level_4: Clearly communicates key reasons for a requested consultation
Communicates concerns and provides feedback to peers and learners
level_5: Clearly and concisely responds to a consultation request
Coordinates recommendations from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care

level_1: Accurately records information in the electronic health record (EHR) in a timely manner
Appropriately selects and uses direct (e.g., telephone, in-person) and indirect (e.g., progress notes, texts, and inbox messages) forms of communication based on context
level_2: Safeguards protected health information by using appropriate communication channels
Communicates clearly, concisely, and in an organized written form, including anticipatory guidance
level_3: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the EHR
Provides written or verbal communication (e.g., patient notes, email) that serves as an example for others to follow
level_4: Uses documentation tools and shortcuts (e.g., copy/paste) accurately and appropriately, per institutional policy
Coaches others to improve written communication
level_5: Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the EHR
Guides departmental or institutional communication around policies and procedures
